signals.headline: Ontario Is Writing Data Centre Grid Rules Into Its Market Rules, for Every Load Above 10 MW
signals.theFact: Ontario’s IESO is moving its technical requirements for large computational loads into the province’s Market Rules, with the proposed amendments going to a webinar on November 19 and the rule change targeted for Q2 2027. The requirements cover connection, reactive power, oscillation, ramp rates and ride-through, and apply to every transmission-connected computational load and to distribution-connected loads above 10 MW.
signals.oceanFallsAngle: Ocean Falls’ sub-10 MW brownfield siting stays under the size where grid operators from B.C. to Ontario are adding competitive calls and new technical obligations for data centres.

signals.headline: Equinix and Fortinet: “AI Isn’t Centralized,” So Security Moves to Where the Data Lives
signals.theFact: Fortinet made its FortiAIGate guardrails available on the Equinix Distributed AI Hub on November 5, a validated reference architecture for AI workloads that span clouds, data centres and edge environments. The companies say it keeps control, management and inspection within customer infrastructure, with no data leaving the environment, to support data residency and sovereignty requirements.
signals.oceanFallsAngle: When the largest interconnection players design for distributed, data-resident AI, an on-premise MicroNode behind an organization’s own firewall in B.C. is the most direct version of that architecture.

signals.headline: Calgary Moves a Step Closer to a Data Centre Freeze Over Water and Power
signals.theFact: Calgary’s executive committee voted 10–3 to send council a motion for a temporary moratorium on new land-use redesignation applications for large-scale data centres, with a staff report on bylaw changes due by March. Mayor Jeromy Farkas backs the pause, citing residents’ worries about electricity bills and the city’s strained water infrastructure, while a Stantec application for a data centre near northeast Calgary’s Redstone neighbourhood continues through review.
signals.oceanFallsAngle: Ocean Falls keeps each site under 10 MW on already-zoned brownfield industrial land, so it doesn’t depend on the large-scale land-use redesignations Calgary is moving to pause.

signals.headline: Swiss Re: Hyperscale Data Centres Can’t Place the Insurance Limits Their Lenders Require
signals.theFact: Swiss Re P&C reinsurance chief underwriting officer Gianfranco Lot told the Singapore International Reinsurance Conference on November 4 that there isn’t enough capacity for data centres, leaving owners unable to place the limits required under their debt financing. With tens of billions in values on single sites and 90–95% of that risk passed on to reinsurers, Swiss Re is talking to alternative capital providers to cover peak data centre losses.
signals.oceanFallsAngle: Ocean Falls’ distributed sub-10 MW sites spread value across many small locations instead of one accumulation point, and its AI Infrastructure Captive Program gives owners a structure for the risks conventional capacity won’t absorb.

signals.headline: Alberta Data Centres Have Asked for 26,849 MW, More Than Double the Province’s Record Peak
signals.theFact: Data centre developers had asked to connect 26,849 MW of new load to Alberta’s grid by October, more than double the province’s all-time peak demand of 12,785 MW, and AESO’s entire 1,200 MW interim limit went to just two projects. The Circuit’s four-province comparison finds Alberta, Quebec, Ontario and B.C. all now rationing or repricing data centre power, with B.C. capping new data centre supply at 400 MW over two years and no public list yet of who won it.
signals.oceanFallsAngle: Ocean Falls targets sub-10 MW brownfield sites that stay outside B.C.’s ≥10 MW competitive call and connect through BC Hydro’s standard process, instead of joining a multi-gigawatt queue for rationed power.

signals.headline: Sherbrooke Delays a Data Centre Freeze as 12,000 Sign Against a 96 MW Campus
signals.theFact: Sherbrooke Mayor Marie-Claude Bibeau kept a proposed data centre moratorium off Tuesday’s council agenda, saying the city needs more time to weigh its legal and technical impacts. Residents are fighting a 96 MW project by U.S.-backed Keel Infrastructure on land the city conditionally sold in August, with a petition against the sale topping 12,000 signatures and two more crypto-to-AI conversions in the works.
signals.oceanFallsAngle: Ocean Falls keeps each site under 10 MW on already-zoned brownfield industrial land, a footprint small enough to avoid the scale that turns a municipal land sale into a 12,000-signature fight.
